answer_text:
The evidence is mixed and depends on the specific metric and dataset used. Regarding hallucination rates, most studies indicate that retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) reduces hallucinated content, though one study found it increased hallucinations and another found no measurable reduction. Specifically, [S010, 0-1218], [S006, 0-1219], and [S008, 0-1267] report that RAG clearly reduces hallucinated content. In contrast, [S012, 0-1012] states that RAG increases hallucinated content, and [S007, 0-609] reports that RAG does not measurably reduce hallucinated content.

Regarding answer accuracy, the results are also conflicting. One study found that RAG makes answers clearly more accurate [S020, 0-1268]. However, another study found that RAG makes generated answers less accurate [S013, 0-1113]. Detailed results from [S013, 1113-2412] show that on the SciFactBench dataset, the retrieval-augmented generator had a lower answer accuracy (62.2%) compared to the vanilla LLM (66.3%), and on PopCultureQA, it scored 7.2 percentage points lower than the vanilla LLM in answer accuracy.
